stemBlocks.value: Three matrices are given: A = (1 0 / 0 1), B = (2 −1 4 / 3 0 5) and C = (7 2 / −3 6). (a) State which matrix is the identity matrix. (b) State which matrix is rectangular. (c) State the order of EACH matrix.
Think first: Identify each matrix by its shape and by the pattern of its entries — no arithmetic is needed at all.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p194-q02 from workbook page 194.

solutionSteps.instruction: Look for 1s on the leading diagonal and 0s everywhere else.

contentBlocks.value: A has 1, 1 down the diagonal from top left, with 0s off it.
Result: A is the identity matrix

solutionSteps.instruction: Find the matrix whose row count differs from its column count.
Count rows then columns for each matrix.

contentBlocks.value: A: 2 rows, 2 columns. B: 2 rows, 3 columns. C: 2 rows, 2 columns.
Result: A is 2 × 2, B is 2 × 3, C is 2 × 2

strategyBlocks.value: Look for the square matrix with 1s down the leading diagonal and 0s elsewhere, then count rows and columns for each matrix.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (a) A is the identity matrix  (b) B is rectangular  (c) A is of order 2 × 2, B is of order 2 × 3, and C is of order 2 × 2.

whyThisWorks.value: The identity matrix must be square and carry 1s only on the leading diagonal, because that is the pattern that leaves any conformable matrix unchanged when multiplied. C is square too, but its entries do not fit the pattern, so it is not the identity. Shape alone settles which matrix is rectangular.

commonErrors.misconception: Calling C the identity because it is square.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Calling C the identity because it is square.

commonErrors.misconception: Describing B as 3 × 2 by counting columns first.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Describing B as 3 × 2 by counting columns first.

commonErrors.misconception: Thinking a matrix of 0s is the identity — that is the zero matrix.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Thinking a matrix of 0s is the identity — that is the zero matrix.

examTip.value: The identity matrix is the matrix version of the number 1: square, with 1s on the diagonal, and it leaves other matrices unchanged under multiplication.
